# University of Melbourne
Established by Act of Incorporation in January 1853, the University of Melbourne began classes in 1855 and is one of Australia’s oldest and most prestigious institutions. It was initially endowed with funds from the gold rush era and opened with faculties in arts, medicine, law, and music. A law school was established in 1857, followed by engineering and medicine in the early 1860s. Women were admitted starting in 1881, marking an early progressive step in Australian education. The university expanded through the 20th century, incorporating several tertiary colleges and growing its student population beyond 35,000 by the 1990s. In 2008, it introduced the “Melbourne Model,” transitioning from specialist undergraduate degrees to a two-degree structure with generalist bachelor’s degrees followed by graduate specialization, sparking some controversy among staff and students.
The main Parkville campus is complemented by others in Burnley, Southbank, Werribee, and regional Victoria. The university maintains diverse faculties including Arts, Science, Engineering, Medicine, Law, and Fine Arts, and is affiliated with the Melbourne Business School. Governance is overseen by a 13-member council, with faculty deans and senior administrators leading academic programs. The university has a strong research profile, with expenditures second only to the CSIRO in Australia, and numerous research centers. It has a substantial endowment (~$1.335 billion) and undertakes significant fundraising campaigns to support growth and infrastructure development.
The University of Melbourne is internationally ranked as Australia’s top university and holds high global positions (#19 QS 2026; #37 THE 2026). It boasts notable alumni, including several Australian prime ministers, Nobel laureates, scientists, artists, and public figures. Student life includes two main student unions, over 200 clubs, and extensive sports programs managed by Melbourne University Sport. The university has nine affiliated residential colleges primarily around the cricket oval at the northern campus edge and offers a rich cultural environment with multiple museums and galleries, such as the Grainger Museum and Ian Potter Museum of Art. Recent years have seen demographic growth in international students (44% of total), workforce casualization issues, campus protests related to political causes, and ongoing campus expansion projects, including a new engineering campus at Fishermans Bend planned for 2026.
In summary, the University of Melbourne is a comprehensive research-intensive institution with a rich history, broad academic offerings, significant cultural assets, and a leading role in Australian and international higher education.
